# Today on Hacker News

## 🤖 AI & Machine Learning
The AI conversation is buzzing today. **"Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit"** offers a firsthand look at the latest developments from one of Europe's leading AI labs, while **"Liquid AI reveals 8B-A1B MoE trained on 38T"** highlights a new Mixture-of-Experts model trained on a staggering 38 trillion tokens — a sign of just how rapidly the frontier is advancing. On the tooling side, **"Show HN: Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA"** showcases a community-built inference engine aimed at squeezing maximum performance out of LLMs. More provocatively, **"MCP Is Dead"** questions the longevity of the Model Context Protocol, and **"Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots"** raises eyebrows about the creative (and ethically murky) ways companies are collecting real-world training data for robotic AI.

## 💻 Programming & Engineering
Developers had plenty to chew on today. **"SQLite is all you need for durable workflows"** makes a compelling case for leaning on the humble embedded database for serious production workloads — a perennial HN crowd-pleaser. **"Bijou64: A variable-length integer encoding"** dives into the elegant low-level design decisions behind a new integer encoding scheme from Ink & Switch. **"On Rendering Diffs"** explores the surprisingly deep UX and algorithmic challenges of displaying code diffs well. And **"You can just say it"** — a post from Redis creator antirez — encourages developers to communicate more directly and plainly, a message that resonated with the community.

## 🌐 Tech & Society
Some of the most-discussed stories today sit at the intersection of technology and the broader world. **"The dead economy theory"** is the day's highest-scoring post, sparking nearly 800 comments with its provocative take on economic stagnation in the digital age. **"Is AI causing a repeat of frontend's lost decade?"** draws a sharp parallel between today's AI-generated web and the bloated, framework-heavy era of the 2010s — a thread that clearly struck a nerve. Meanwhile, **"The California state assembly has passed the 'Protect Our Games Act'"** marks a significant legislative win for the Stop Killing Games movement, requiring publishers to keep games playable even after official support ends.

## 🔧 Hardware & Other
On the hardware front, **"It's hard to justify buying a Framework 12"** gives an honest, measured review of the new compact modular laptop, concluding that while the concept is admirable, the value proposition is tough to defend at its price point. Rounding things out, **"Print with dozens of colors: Our new open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer"** is a treat for 3D printing enthusiasts, with Prusa Research releasing an open-source multi-color mixing feature for their popular slicing software. Finally, **"Free full BGP feed. IPv4 and IPv6"** is a quiet but useful gem for network engineers looking for free routing table data.
